posts.cooked:
More and more, the world is moving toward agentic AI usage. It’s reasonable to assume that the vast majority of people on this forum have already used tools like ChatGPT in some capacity — even if only in a non-agentic way.

Technology is evolving quickly, and expectations are evolving with it. I believe it’s time for Blizzard Entertainment to consider introducing a structured AI integration strategy for World of Warcraft — starting with two components:

An In-Game AI Assistant (LLM-Based)

An in-game assistant trained specifically on WoW data could provide contextual, intelligent support such as:

  • “Where can I farm cloth efficiently at my level?”

  • “Based on my character’s gear and spec, what Mythic+ difficulty is reasonable?”

  • “What’s the fastest way to unlock X reputation?”

This wouldn’t replace gameplay. It would enhance decision-making and reduce friction — especially for returning players or those navigating increasingly complex systems.

Think of it as a modern evolution of in-game help systems — but dynamic, personalized, and aware of your character.

A Structured MCP Server for External Agent Integration

Looking one step further: a properly designed MCP-style interface that allows controlled, compliant agent interaction.

Not botting. Not automation of combat. Not “run this delve for me.”

But reasonable quality-of-life actions such as:

  • Navigating from point A to point B

  • Guiding a character to a profession trainer

  • Bringing a player to the entrance of a specific instance

For example:

“Take me to the Tailoring trainer in Silvermoon.”
“Bring me to the entrance of X dungeon.”

This would be structured, logged, rule-bound, and aligned with the Terms of Service — not an open door to abuse.

Why This Matters

The world is changing. Software is changing. Workflows are changing.

Games don’t need to resist this shift — they can shape it.

Right now, players alt-tab constantly to look up guides, routes, builds, and farming spots. An integrated AI layer would keep players immersed instead of pushing them to third-party sites.

Even starting small — just an interactive LLM inside the game trained on WoW knowledge — would be a strong first step. MCP-style extensibility could follow once governance and guardrails are clear.

A Cultural Perspective

In many industries, AI copilots are already standard. Very few professionals today write important emails, reports, or proposals without at least running them past an AI assistant. It’s not about replacing humans — it’s about augmenting capability.

Gaming will not be an exception to this broader transformation.

WoW has always evolved — from add-ons to group finder to cross-realm systems. AI integration feels like the next logical step in that progression.

If done thoughtfully and transparently, it could strengthen the ecosystem rather than disrupt it.
